title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff ordering (regional failover race)
description: Background: During a recent incident we observed the SLO enforcer backoff + regional failover path could reorder pending requests when regions recovered concurrently, causing premature load-shedding and unnecessary circuit trips. This PR fixes a race in the failover ordering logic and hardens the enforcer to ensure deterministic ordering across regions. Motivation: Customers experienced increased 5xx and degraded latency after regional flaps. The root cause was traced to a non-deterministic enqueuing order in the regional failover coordinator combined with a later backoff update that reorders in-flight tokens. This change stabilizes ordering and prevents the enforcer from over-shedding during recovery. Changes: (high level) - Add per-request monotonic sequence numbers on failover tokens and use them to preserve ordering during cross-region merges. - Move backoff window updates to happen-before the queue merge to avoid reorder races. - Add a small bounded in-memory buffer to preserve order when regions reconnect briefly. - Add unit and integration tests that reproduce the previous race condition and validate fix. - Tune the canary and chaos tests to surface regressions. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests covering sequence number logic - [x] Integration test simulating concurrent regional recovery - [x] Bench sanity run (basic throughput and latency) - [x] Add release_notes entry Rollout plan: - Deploy to canary first (us-west-2), monitor SLO enforcement and shed metrics for 30m. - Widen rollout to global after 1h if no regressions. - If regressions, revert via rollback tag (instructions in ops runbook). Related: Linear ENG-2041, ENG-2075; Incident: SUP-9876. Notes: The behavioral change is focused on ordering consistency; no change to declared thresholds or default backoff constants. The small buffer is configurable and off by default; it's enabled in this hotfix to stabilize recovery more quickly.
author: Maya Chen
